source.title: Architect of the Bits World: Masked Autoregressive Modeling for Circuit Generation Guided by Truth Table
source.authors: Haoyuan Wu; Haisheng Zheng; Shoubo Hu; Zhuo-Lun He; Bei Yu

record.tranche_reason: The study reports model-size, training-token and compute scaling results for CircuitAR on circuit generation, a different task and system from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The scaling results use Bits Distance (BitsD), the MAE between an untrained CircuitNN initialized from CircuitAR and truth-table labels—not held-out cross-entropy. The paper does not test language-model loss scaling or the stated language-model compute-optimal allocation. Reported circuit-generation efficiency and accuracy results after DAS are not rows because they do not measure the scaling behavior in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains CircuitAR masked-autoregressive circuit generators at 300M–2B parameters and 1B–4B tokens and reports how its BitsD metric scales with parameters, tokens and compute. This is a new setting for V5. It is weak evidence: BitsD is a task-error metric (MAE of an untrained CircuitNN versus truth-table labels), not held-out training loss. The range is under one order of magnitude, and the 'power-law relationship' is asserted without a fitted exponent.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim CircuitAR shows scalability following a power law, plus emergent capability in generating complex circuits. They also call the scaling-law investigation preliminary, limited by compute to restricted model and data sizes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses masked autoregressive circuit generation and BitsD rather than language-model training and held-out cross-entropy; it reports scaling trends but no fitted loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported BitsD varies with model size, training-token amount and compute. Appendix E also reports that BitsD changes with the proportion of isolated NAND gates, with the 300M model more affected than the 2B model.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed compute, larger CircuitAR models reach lower BitsD despite fewer tokens (Figure 5). The text also reports better data efficiency: 2B with 4B tokens beats 1B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In non-text generative domains, compute-optimal allocation favours larger models over more tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Circuit depth rises sharply at 2B versus 1B, and NAND count drops at 2B, which the authors call an emergent phase transition (Figure 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structural capabilities emerge abruptly at a scale threshold in circuit-generation models.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is on circuit-generation models and BitsD rather than held-out language-model loss. The reported model and token ranges are limited; the paper calls the investigation preliminary and notes computational constraints. It provides no fitted exponents or uncertainty estimates, and some scaling comparisons are described qualitatively or shown in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling rows were extracted from figure-only intermediate points because their values are not stated in the text. Circuit-generation benchmark accuracy, DAS steps, NAND counts and the initialization ablation were left out because they do not measure a version's scaling behavior.

untested.parts: No held-out training loss is measured. There is no fitted power law, no exponents, and the range is under one order of magnitude rather than several. Image/video, repeated data and fine-tuning/transfer are not tested.
No language models or held-out text pretraining loss.
No compute-optimal allocation law for language models. The fixed-compute comparison in circuits is qualitative only.
Shape is varied together with size (Table 3), never at a fixed parameter count.
Downstream IWLS results use only CircuitAR-2B, not a scale sweep.
No variation of fitting or setup choices.

missing.what: Stated per-step improvements in BitsD: 7.94% for 0.3B→0.6B versus 6.07% for 1B→2B (diminishing returns). These are the only quantitative evidence on the curve's shape.
Intermediate 600M and 1B BitsD points and per-size token curves are figure-only (Figures 4 and 6). They are needed to judge the power-law form.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence for V5 is weak. BitsD is a task-error metric, not loss. Only four model sizes spanning under one order of magnitude are tested. The power law is asserted by citing Kaplan without any fit, and no uncertainty is reported. Architecture shape co-varies with size. The reader's 'partial' states on baseline endpoints (r1, r3) were mislabelled.

versions.untested_parts: No language models or held-out pretraining cross-entropy; BitsD on circuit-generation models is a different measure.
No test of small-run fits predicting much larger runs.
No search for a loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation at fixed compute or test of how that allocation grows with compute.
No comparison of depth, width or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count for the claimed loss.
Tests scaling in circuit generation using BitsD, not the same held-out-loss measure; does not test image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
No downstream task performance scaling or relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
Does not vary parameter-counting, fitting method, training schedule or other setup choices to test fitted-exponent dependence or curve bending.

rows.subject: CircuitAR-300M
rows.operation_detail: Compared BitsD across CircuitAR parameter sizes.
rows.note: One endpoint of the reported model-size sweep; the text says the progression follows a power-law relationship.
rows.check: This is the 300M baseline endpoint of the parameter sweep, so on its own it shows no effect. It should serve as the baseline for r2, not carry a 'partial' state.

rows.subject: CircuitAR-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared BitsD across CircuitAR parameter sizes.
rows.note: The paper reports this as the endpoint after scaling from 300M parameters; it describes the progression as a power law and says marginal returns diminish at larger scales.
rows.check: Baseline should be 0.5317 (300M, r1), not 'not stated'. BitsD falls monotonically to 0.4362 at 2B. The power-law form is asserted, not fitted, and the range is about 0.8 orders of magnitude.

rows.subject: CircuitAR-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared BitsD after training on different token amounts.
rows.note: The text gives this value as the starting point for the 2B model's comparison from 1B to 4B training tokens.
rows.check: This is the 1B-token starting point for the 2B model and only the baseline for r4. A single value shows no effect.

rows.subject: CircuitAR-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared BitsD after training on different token amounts.
rows.note: The paper reports an 8.13% improvement from 0.4748 to 0.4362 when scaling the 2B model from 1B to 4B tokens.
rows.check: Baseline should be 0.4748 (2B model at 1B tokens). The 8.13% drop shows improvement with more data, but there is no power-law fit across only a 4× range of tokens.

rows.subject: CircuitAR model-size comparison
rows.operation_detail: Compared BitsD across model sizes under a fixed compute budget.
rows.value: The paper states that larger models achieve better performance despite training on fewer tokens, and that BitsD scales inversely with the computing budget.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison reported for the model-size sweep; the text does not provide the plotted values.
rows.check: Qualitative only, with values in Figure 5 at 1.38–9.24 GFLOPs/token. The paper says BitsD 'scales inversely with the computing budget'. The claim that larger models do better at fixed compute is an allocation-type finding outside text LMs, which no version covers as stated (V3 is about LM loss).

relationships.condition: CircuitAR circuit generation, BitsD metric, 300M–2B parameters and 1B–4B tokens
relationships.reason: BitsD falls monotonically with parameters (0.5317→0.4362, r1–r2), tokens (0.4748→0.4362, r3–r4) and compute (r5). Returns diminish with size, consistent with a power law, but no fit is reported and the range is narrow.
relationships.display_finding: BitsD decreased from 0.5317 to 0.4362 with parameters and from 0.4748 to 0.4362 with tokens, also improving with compute, with diminishing returns but no power-law fit.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
